newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BONDS FROZEN ON AMBIGUITY OVER TAX ISSUES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BONDS FROZEN ON AMBIGUITY OVER TAX ISSUES.

text.p: Greek secondary bond market trading had come to a standstill on Tuesday with banks quoting wide bid-ask spreads due to uncertainty over tax issues, traders said.
One-week implied drachma rates from forex forwards were firmer in early trade as some players were seeking funding for recently auctioned bonds and FRNs.
Ecu/drachma was trading lower below 304 on a perky dollar.
"Bond trading in the secondary market has come to a halt with banks quoting wide spreads as uncertainty over tax issues has set in," said a dealer at a private bank.

The trader said banks had yet to agree whether the 7.5 percent tax on interest earned from state securities would be reflected on clean prices or on accrual interest when banks transacted with each other.
"There is a meeting today at the Union of Greek banks to find a common solution to the problem," said a bond dealer.
Other bond dealers blamed the finance ministry for being late in explaining how foreign investors would claim the tax paid on Greek bonds.
Money dealers said implied drachma rates from forex forwards in one-week period firmed 10 to 20 bassi points as some foreign banks were seeking funding for recently auctioned bonds and floaters.

The auction of 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 12.40 percent produced an average accepted bid of 101.04. Another 75 billion drachmas were allocated in non-competitive bids.

The auction of the three-year, 10.20 percent coupon bond produced an average accepted bid of 99.91. The finance ministry allocated 120 billion drachmas in competitive bid and 36 billion drachmas in non-competitive bids.
The mark was quoted at 156.50/60 drachmas from Monday's 156.560 fix, the dollar at 258.76/86 drachmas from 256.320 and the Ecu at 303.85/95 from 303.900 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is softer trading below 304," said a forex dealer. "This is primarily due to a very strong dollar."
The National Bank of Greece, the domestic money market's biggest player, quoted the following early rates:
** Overnight at 11.90-12.40
** One week at 11.90-12.40
** Two weeks at 11.80-12.30
** Three weeks at 11.70-12.20
** One month at 11.60-12.10
** Two months at 11.55-12.05
** Three months at 11.40-11.90
** Six months at 11.20-11.70
** Nine months at 11.10-11.60
** Twelve months at 11.00-11.50
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
